reason: The cited evidence (E1) concerns C and Mo microalloying in a CoCrFeNi-based HEA, showing FCC phase stabilization and improved ductility, but it does not involve Ti, NbMoTaW, or irradiation. None of the key premises about Ti-induced phase formation, twinning mechanisms, or property retention in NbMoTaW are supported by this or any other cited passage.
premises: Minor Ti addition (~2 at.%) to NbMoTaW can induce a ductile FCC or nanodomain phase.
The induced phase activates additional slip systems or twinning at room temperature.
The BCC matrix remains dominant to preserve high-temperature strength.
Irradiation resistance is not compromised by the minor phase change.
Ti lowers stacking fault energy locally to promote twinning or slip.
